observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a front view of a heavy creature. A tall fan of olive-green backswept ridged plates with wavy tips rises above a round head with a broad chin. The head has two small red eyes set high. The animal stands on four thick, grey-olive, wrinkled columnar legs. East: a side profile, clearly lower and smaller than south. A long, level, spiked tail runs left. A domed shell of many backswept wavy-tipped plates sits over four tall wrinkled legs, clear of the ground. A long horizontal striped neck runs right and ends in a flat duck-billed snout with raised red eyes. North: a rear view. A fan of plates shows two small knobs (the back of the head and its eye bumps) above the top. A spiked tail hangs down the middle toward the camera. The legs match south.
observed.south.png: Front view of the creature. A radiating fan of tall ridged olive and yellow-green shell plates curls at the tips. A round, short-snouted head sits low in the middle with two red eyes on top and a wide flat mouth. Four massive wrinkled elephant-like legs with toe nails. Painterly and naturalistic, clean alpha. The face is somewhat broad and fleshy, but not cute.
observed.east.png: Side profile: a long body raised high on four columnar wrinkled legs. A domed shell of overlapping backswept plates with blunt wavy spines, like a frilled crest. A long, level, horizontal neck with yellow-green and olive stripes. A flat duck-billed snout with small raised red eyes. A long, thin, level tail with a row of small spikes on top. Natural texture and lighting, clean alpha, no ground shadow.
observed.north.png: Rear view: a fan of backswept plates. A small ridged dome with two knobs (back of the head and eye bumps, no visible eyes) sits at the top. The tail with a central row of spikes hangs down toward the viewer, ending in small spikes. Thick wrinkled hind legs with nails. Palette matches the other facings, clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the shiro sits in a cell beside the vanilla human: about one cell long, a little shorter than the human. At 32 px per cell it reads as a spiky green shell on legs with a tail, distinct from the ground and larger than the rat.

request.subject: RSW_Shiro

edits.change: All facings share one scale: the shell dome stands the same height on every view, about 60% of the sprite's full height, and the four columnar legs are the same length and thickness in every view, with the feet on the same ground line.

The east facing is a true side profile of the same animal at the same physical size as south and north: the shell fills the same share of the canvas height, with the head at the front, the tail at the rear and two thick weight-bearing legs visible beneath the shell.

Every view is composed to fill the canvas to the same extent, with the animal's top edge and its feet touching the same rows. The side view is wider than it is tall, and its height equals the height of the front and rear views.

invariants: Hard-shelled, benign, slow-moving reptile with a heavy domed shell, thick columnar legs, a blunt head and a short tail
Spines rising from the shell, the same count and size in every view
One palette across all facings: olive-brown shell with darker plate seams, pale tan spines, muted green-grey skin
Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic proportions, clean dark outline, transparent background
South is the front view with the head and eyes toward the viewer; north is the rear view seen from behind, showing the shell, tail and haunches with the eyes hidden; east is the side profile
request.prompt: A Shiro, a hard-shelled, benign, slow-moving reptile native to Naboo, drawn as a RimWorld creature sprite in a painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, with a clean dark outline on a transparent background. The body is a heavy domed shell on four thick columnar legs, with a blunt reptilian head on a short neck and a short tail. Rows of sharp, pale tan spines rise from the shell, the same number and size in every view. The shell is olive-brown with darker plate seams, and the skin is muted green-grey. Three facings are drawn at one shared scale as the same animal at the same physical size. The shell dome stands the same height in every view, about 60% of the sprite's full height. The four legs are the same length and thickness in every view, with the feet on the same ground line, and the top of the shell and the feet reach the same rows of the canvas in every facing. South: front view, the head and eyes toward the viewer, the shell rising behind the head and two thick forelegs planted below. North: rear view, seen from behind, showing the back of the shell, the tail and the haunches, with the eyes hidden. East: true side profile, wider than it is tall, with the head at the front, the tail at the rear and two thick weight-bearing legs beneath the shell. The shell, torso and legs on the east view match the south and north views in height and thickness, so the east shiro is as large as the others.
